A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dial-In LLM, with matching core experiments and identifiable revisions. All 11 pages of v2 and 14 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original Chinese intent-clustering experiments, LLM evaluation and naming accuracies, downstream classification results, sampling analyses and proprietary-model comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds English benchmark evaluations, numerical-scoring experiments and cluster-merging ablations.

M1.justification: v2 describes merging clusters using a label-distance threshold. v3 Section 3.3 introduces normalized label embeddings, geodesic affinity edges, a von Mises–Fisher mixture filter, connected-component merging and relabeling. Algorithm 1 also changes the selection ratio to good/(bad+1) and replaces the bad-cluster stopping condition with a remaining-sentence proportion and iteration cap.

E1.justification: v3 adds actual English evaluations on Bank77, CLINC(I), MTOP(I) and Massive(I), extending beyond the Chinese customer-service evaluation in v2. English datasets listed descriptively in v2 were not evaluated there. The Chinese dataset remains 55,085 sentences and 1,507 intents.

E2.justification: The Chinese comparison in Table 2 adds LLMEdgeRefine. The new English comparison introduces SCCL and Self-supervise alongside previously evaluated methods; LLMEdgeRefine has results for three English datasets, with Bank77 left blank. Existing Chinese comparators and appendix proprietary-model comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include Llama-7B fine-tuning on 800 English clusters, numerical-scoring training/testing on 1,000/200 clusters, and a Bank77 cost comparison using three iterations over candidate counts {10,30,50,70}. The stated Chinese utilities change from Qwen14B for both functions to Qwen14B and ChatGLM3-6B. Appendix A revises the initial source count from over 120,000 to over 11,879 calls; these disclosures do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds binary-versus-four-level coherence scoring, a comparison crossing cosine/geodesic distance with deterministic/probabilistic merging, and comparative LLM-call accounting. These investigate additional design and efficiency questions. Original sampling, crowdsourcing and search-pruning analyses remain, although the detailed ChatGLM random-sampling breakdown is removed.

E5.justification: The new numerical-scoring study specifies five judgments per cluster, majority aggregation and disagreement analysis. This adds limited repeated-judgment reporting, without establishing an increase in independent experimental runs. Neither version reports seed-level variability, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing Chinese result entries and appendix proprietary-model accuracies remain unchanged. New results include LLMEdgeRefine at 0.7411 NMI/87.2% goodness and merge-only at 0.8420/97.8%, English scores leading only on Massive(I), numerical-scoring accuracies of 58.5–65%, merging ablations, and estimated call counts of 480 versus 1,024 and 3,080. The ChatGLM random-sampling rows accompanying v2 Figure 2 disappear; the plotted sampling results remain.

T1.justification: v3 substantially extends the mathematical formulation beyond v2's generic distance threshold: it defines hyperspherical embeddings, geodesic affinity graphs and a von Mises–Fisher mixture expression with uniform weights. The local-search objective also gains a denominator offset. These introduce substantive definitions and assumptions, although no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v3 adds comparative computational efficiency to the abstract and conclusion and narrows the abstract's outlook from general human-aligned problem-solving to intent clustering. The dataset, human-alignment and clustering-quality contributions remain. The 12% downstream improvement disappears from the abstract but remains in Section 5.4.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations favoring binary judgments, geodesic distance and probabilistic merging, plus an efficiency argument based on fewer LLM calls. Its new Limitations section discusses coherence overlooking meaningfulness and granularity, restricted Chinese/domain coverage, and unaddressed intent trajectories and document-level tasks. These substantially expand v2's brief discussion of future confidence estimation.

D1.justification: v3 adds disclosures including four A100 GPUs, 20-sentence naming clusters and LLM inputs, explicit checkpoint links, and merging thresholds of 0.8 and 0.7. It also clarifies the proprietary-model evaluation set and Qwen version. Both PDFs retain the same sample-data repository link and defer full dataset/model release until acceptance.

R1.justification: v3 adds supporting citations including Banerjee, Fletcher, Chen, FitzGerald, Khan and Vinh, while removing the Hong 2024 chatbot paper and Liu 2024 OpenEval reference. Positioning still emphasizes intermediate clustering results, with additional criticism of prior methods' cost and uncertainty. The retitled Hong 2025 reference represents the same linked work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Preliminaries are integrated into Proposed Methods, the context-free/context-aware hierarchy becomes utility/iteration/merging/role subsections, implementation information is consolidated, and appendix B is split into B and C. The author and affiliation block also changes.

P2.justification: v3 adds the framework overview in Figure 2 and three result tables, expands Tables 1–2, and reformats Algorithm 1 with highlighted LLM evaluation. The unchanged sampling plot moves into the main text at a smaller size, losing its accompanying numerical table. Appendix example tables and iteration logs are relocated and renumbered rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: English benchmarks, targeted ablations and explicit limitations strengthen validation and transparency. However, v3 replaces the simple merging rule with an underspecified construction: Section 3.3 labels a density-product mixture a conditional probability without posterior normalization and leaves its concentration parameter unspecified. Appendix A also changes the source count to over 11,879 calls without reconciling the retained over-100,000 claim. These new methodological and provenance concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment despite the useful additions.
